key_highlights: ASX 200 closed the week higher despite intraday volatility driven by RBA rate-hike speculation; Qantas lifted while Wesfarmers and Sigma slumped
Housing market under severe stress: auction sentiment deteriorating, 'perfect storm' warnings, and housing inflation remains a persistent RBA constraint
Pilbara mining activity booming; Gateway Resources adds 7km gold trend in WA; small-caps X2M, Discovery Alaska, Metal Hawk, Bapcor lead ASX runners
Jackson Hole Fed summit with Kevin Warsh keynote adds global rate-path uncertainty; Trump-Venezuela oil deal introduces energy supply volatility
Qantas faces operational strain (Sydney delays, sacked workers) but fuel hedging and new fleet shield margins; Virgin similarly protected
Australia imposes 'high bar' for fossil-fuel-powered data centres, signalling energy transition policy tightening

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely to range-trade with elevated volatility. Rate-hike headlines and housing stress cap upside; Pilbara mining strength and small-cap momentum provide support. Jackson Hole outcome is the key swing factor. Expect 1-2% weekly swings.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA holds and housing stabilises. Materials sector benefits from commodity strength. Energy transition policy and AI capex cycles create structural opportunities. Key risk is a housing correction spilling into bank credit losses.
